intelligence.bindingDescription: Disabled by default; available only when the credential agent is enabled. Match assets and credentials against captured traffic, link real requests or responses, and save matching excerpts. This does not attempt login or treat matching traffic as successful verification. Disabling the agent also disables linking; existing links are retained.
intelligence.agentDescription: Disabled by default. Independently process existing and new credentials, separating and highlighting usernames, passwords, tokens, and cookies without changing original reports or verification status. Complex text uses additional model tokens; parseable JSON does not require a model. Enable automatic recording first. Configure the model under Agents → Credential processing.
intelligence.recordDescription: Disabled by default. Reporting credentials, leads, and sensitive data increases task agent prompt and reporting token usage. This records data without starting credential processing. Disabling also turns off the agent and traffic linking below; existing intelligence and processed results remain available.
intelligence.description: Record credentials, important leads, and sensitive data found during tasks, preserving source evidence.

experimental.description:
Experimental mechanisms are disabled by default. They may change agent behavior or affect stability; enable them only after understanding the impact.

noa context compaction lets the model compact long conversation histories (norma v0.4.0). The four agent types (planner / worker / main agent / chat) use noa instead of built-in compaction. Original content is archived in the task workspace for review. Changes apply to subsequent runs without rebuilding agents; disabling restores built-in compaction immediately.

experimental.disabledToast: noa context compaction disabled (built-in compaction restored).

constraints.description:
Include each task's operation constraints (the allow/deny entries maintained in its overview) in the corresponding agent's system prompt to limit exploration, for example to the current port or to prohibit brute force.

Control injection into the planner and worker independently; both default to enabled. Changes apply on the next turn without rebuilding agents. A disabled agent no longer sees the constraints.

proxy.customProbeDescription: The service must return a plain-text IP or JSON in the format '{"ip":"1.2.3.4"}'. If public services are unreachable, or the host and internal proxy share a public IP, use an internal IP probe service. Different IPs for ① and ② confirm that traffic uses the internal proxy.
proxy.testDescription: Test contacts an IP echo service (api.ipify.org by default, with ifconfig.me as fallback) to report the request's source IP. ① is the direct IP; ② is the global proxy IP. Test edited values without saving first.

proxy.description:
All agent target traffic exits through this proxy to hide the source IP or use a relay. Supports http / https / socks5 with optional user:pass authentication. Leave blank for direct connections.

With traffic capture enabled, this is the recording proxy's upstream: traffic is stored before being forwarded. Without capture, it is injected directly into agent bash / WebFetch connections. It is independent of web search and LLM proxies.

Tip: with capture disabled, socks5 depends on each command-line tool supporting ALL_PROXY. curl works, but tools such as Python urllib fail. For socks5, enabling traffic capture is recommended: the MITM proxy handles the connection directly, transparently to tools.

binding.description:
Disabled by default. When enabled, the report agent triggered by a saved finding reviews existing HTTP requests/responses and links matching traffic before writing the report. Reviewing packets and additional tool calls increase token usage.

TCP findings and findings without captured or matching traffic can still be reported. This does not change traffic capture, manual linking, or access to saved evidence. It applies on the next agent turn; disabling immediately rejects new automatic links.
binding.title: Automatic agent traffic linking

traffic.description:
When enabled, all agent HTTP traffic is stored through the recording proxy. Agents receive traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy configuration, including proxy instructions in their prompts.

When disabled (the default), no traffic is recorded. Agents do not receive proxy configuration or traffic tools, and their prompts exclude proxy instructions. Switching immediately rebuilds agents to apply the change.

pool.title: LLM rotation · failover
pool.desc: When on, agents that don't specify a model automatically switch to the next profile whenever the current one is unusable (insufficient balance / expired key / rate limit / service error).

enable.label: Enable rotation
enable.hint: Off by default. When off, only the active profile is ever used, and a failure just fails.

bindFallback.label: Fall back even when a pinned model fails
bindFallback.hint: Off by default: when an agent or task pins a specific profile, only that profile is used and a failure just fails (no silent switch to another model). When on, a pinned profile that fails falls back to the rotation chain below.

pool.note: The active profile is always first; the rest follow in order of priority (set on each profile). When a profile fails it enters a cooldown (60s → 5min → 30min), is skipped during the cooldown, and is automatically brought back once it recovers. Profiles that can't fit the current request in their context window are skipped. Agents and tasks that pin a model don't take part in the rotation by default.

It's for gateways that use a session-id header for prompt caching / sticky routing. The same session stays stable across turns, and different sessions differ from one another. Not sent if empty.

priority.label: Rotation priority
priority.hint: Higher numbers are picked first. The active profile is always first regardless of this value. Profiles with the same priority take turns going first, naturally sharing the quota.

exclude.label: Exclude from rotation
exclude.hint: When on, this profile is never used as a failover target (it can still be used when an agent or task pins it explicitly). Good for an expensive profile you want "reserved for a specific agent, so it isn't consumed when others fail."

streaming.label: Streaming output · streaming
streaming.hint: When on (default), it runs over streaming SSE so you can watch real-time progress and live token counts during a run. When off, it runs truly non-streaming (stream:false, returning the full response at once), which can work around broken SSE implementations on some gateways (empty frames / frames missing the thinking field) but loses real-time progress during a run.

maxTokens.label: Output cap · max tokens
maxTokens.hint: The maximum number of tokens to generate in a single response, sent with every request. 0 (default) = don't send this field and follow the server default. This differs from the "Context window" above, which is the model's total capacity and is used only to compute the compaction threshold locally. Set it too small and a reasoning model gets cut off during the thinking stage and can't answer a single character.

maxTokensFieldHint.openai: Which key to send the cap under. max_tokens is the default and most compatible gateways recognize only this. OpenAI's official reasoning models (the o-series / GPT-5), on the other hand, recognize only max_completion_tokens and throw an unsupported_parameter error the moment they receive max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.anthropic: Selectable only in the openai format. Anthropic's field name is fixed to max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.openai-responses: Selectable only in the openai format. The Responses API's field name is fixed to max_output_tokens.

thinkingType.label: Thinking switch · thinking.type
thinkingType.hint: Controls whether the thinking field is sent. Don't send = omit this field (compatible with models that don't support it, such as MiniMax); Off = send disabled; On = send enabled. Independent of the effort below.

connect.title: Connection retry
connect.trigger: When no connection is made or a 200 hasn't been received yet: network-layer errors such as connection reset / read-write timeout / DNS failure, plus HTTP 408·429·500·502·503·504.
connect.skips: Other status codes (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422, etc.) are definitive rejections that would fail the same way on a resend, so they're passed straight up.
connect.desc: Resends the same request as-is. Once a stream has started (a 200 was already received), this layer no longer handles a mid-stream drop.
connect.offHint: -1 = never retry; pass the failure straight up

empty.title: Empty-response retry
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 with a normal finish_reason of stop, but the entire response contains no content block. Gateway empty frames, frames missing the thinking field, and sampling hiccups all show up this way.
empty.skips: Excludes cases where content is empty because it was cut off by max_tokens (that must be solved by raising the output cap; a resend just hits the same wall again).
empty.desc: It resends the entire prompt, which is costly on long contexts, so it's best not to set the count high.

stream.title: Same-provider safe-window retry
stream.where: This project · before any output is delivered
stream.trigger: A problem that arises after the stream is already established (a 200 was received): a mid-stream disconnect, provider overloaded, or a 429 / 5xx error event inside the stream, while not a single token has yet been delivered to the caller.
stream.skips: Doesn't retry quota exhaustion (402 / insufficient_quota, handled by rotation switching profiles), context overflow (413 / context length, handled by compaction), or the definitive rejections 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422.
stream.desc: Replays the same request on the same profile. Since no output has been delivered yet, replaying doesn't duplicate model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = on a stream drop, hand off immediately to the outer intent re-run layer

breaker.title: Rotation circuit breaker
breaker.where: This project · per process, one global instance
breaker.trigger: Trips when transient failures (429 · 5xx · network errors) pile up consecutively to the threshold. Definitive failures such as insufficient balance (402), expired key (401 / 403), and missing model (404) trip immediately from the first one, ignoring the threshold.
breaker.skips: A single success resets the count to 0, so a profile that only acts up occasionally won't gradually accumulate its way to tripping.
breaker.desc: When tripped, it enters a cooldown, and during the cooldown rotation skips this profile. The state is stored in the DB, so it survives a restart.
breaker.offHint: -1 = never trip on transient failures (definitive failures still trip)

intent.title: Intent re-run
intent.where: This project · per process, one global instance
intent.trigger: When the earlier layers couldn't stop it: a worker ends in model_error. Either the inner retries are all exhausted, or the stream dropped after it had already begun delivering output (replay isn't safe then, so the whole thing has to be run again).
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is already handled by rotation switching profiles, so it isn't re-run here. When a task enters pause / stop / wrap-up, it yields immediately and doesn't take up backoff time.
intent.desc: Runs the entire intent again from the start. As the outermost layer, a single re-run multiplies the counts of all the inner layers once more.
intent.offHint: -1 = don't re-run; mark the intent as blocked right away

retry.emptyLine: Leave empty to use the default. {hint}.

override.label: Retry override
override.hint: Applies to this profile only, overriding the global defaults in "Retry & backoff." Leave a field empty to follow the global value. Enter -1 for the count to turn off this layer's retries. Fill in an interval to use a fixed interval instead of exponential backoff. The circuit breaker and intent re-run are per process, so they can be adjusted only on the global page.

retry.intro: A single model-call failure passes through five retry layers in order from innermost to outermost: <chain>connection → empty response → same-provider safe window → rotation circuit breaker → intent re-run</chain>. An outer layer's turn comes only after the inner one is used up, so the counts <emph>multiply together</emph>. Max out every layer and a single hiccup can burn dozens of requests. Leaving them all empty is the current default, exactly the behavior when this page didn't exist. The first three layers can be overridden individually on each model profile.
